_what: RAIL library vs the live corpus, joined on full InChIKey.

Cholesterol_by_InChIKey_in_CHL_column.asserts: the registry's cholesterol is present as a CHL component

roundtrip_our_own_lead.asserts: the lookup machinery finds AT4-13CRA in our own table when asked, so a zero against the corpus is a real zero and not a broken join

rail_structures_already_in_corpus.interpretation: ZERO is the expected answer and it is now a measured zero rather than an assumed one: no retinoid-derived ionizable lipid has any analogue among the corpus's 19,919 structures. The control above proves the same join finds DLin-MC3-DMA, so the machinery works.

superset_sweep._label: SUPERSET sweep. These counts are chemotype neighbourhoods, NOT shared lipids. The shared-lipid answer is rail_structures_already_in_corpus above.

benchmark_Dlin_MC3.token_pattern_note: The paper's own spelling 'Dlin-MC3' matches 0 corpus rows by name while the molecule is present thousands of times. Joining on IL_name would have reported this benchmark absent.

in_vivo_shared_lipid.why_this_matters: EXTRACTION_BRIEF 5: the in-vivo pool has exactly TWO structures shared across experiments, DLin-MC3-DMA and SM-102. Any in-vivo lipid already present elsewhere is rare and load-bearing.
in_vivo_shared_lipid.what_KJ_2026_would_add: Dlin-MC3 measured in BOTH liver and spleen at 0.1 mg/kg IV, 6 h. LIVER: a FOURTH liver source for MC3 (today NG_2025_2, ZC_2023, ZH_2023), i.e. 3 new organ-matched cross-source pairs on the one benchmark the in-vivo pool actually shares. SPLEEN: the FIRST MC3 spleen measurement anywhere in the in-vivo corpus.

spleen_coverage_today.note: The entire in-vivo corpus has ONE spleen source, ZH_2023. KJ_2026 would be the second. ZH_2023 carries MC3 only in liver, so the two spleen sources would still share no lipid -- the gain is organ coverage, not a new shared-lipid pair.

already_merged_arm_check.verdict: No arm of this paper is in the corpus. KJ_2026 is free; checked by PMID, not by the year token (F-075).
